items.title: Mississauga councillors want to pause data centre builds for a year. Here's why
items.summary: With data centre builds remaining a hot-topic in Ontario municipalities, some Mississauga city councillors are concerned about the uncertainty surrounding what the centres could mean for the community and the environment.

items.title: Two centuries of history: Leslie Log House celebrates 200 years
items.summary: Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House remains a treasured link to Mississauga's early settlement history. Entertainment and activities | July 31, 2026 Members of the media and public are invited to attend a special celebration marking the 200th anniversary of the Leslie Log House, one of the oldest remaining log homes in Ontario. The event will recognize the site’s historical significance and its role in preserving Mississauga’s early settler history. m. m. Community programming continues including a tea room, art in the park and more! Members of Council, representatives from the City of Mississauga and the Streetsville Historical Society, along with community members and heritage enthusiasts. Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House is one of the oldest surviving log homes in Ontario and a designated heritage property. Operated in partnership with the Streetsville Historical Society, the house offers visitors a glimpse into life in early Upper Canada and serves as an important reminder of Mississauga’s rural and agricultural roots. More information on the Leslie Log House can be found on the City’s webpage. ca 905-615-3200, ext.

items.title: Student entrepreneurs gear up for IDEA Connect Summer Market
items.summary: From custom nails and baked goods to creative media, Mississauga's young business owners have something for everyone. On August 12, the IDEA Connect Summer Market will present an event at IDEA Square One that features 13 student-run businesses. Visitors can shop for unique products and services, meet the young business owners behind them and support local talent. The event is a chance to connect, discover something new and celebrate the next generation of entrepreneurs. The young business owners are part of Summer Company, a program funded by the Government of Ontario. People ages 15 to 29 start and run their own businesses during the summer months. High school students commit to 280 or more hours while post-secondary students commit to 420 or more hours between May and Labour Day. Through training, guidance from IDEA and hands-on experience, they build skills and turn their ideas into real businesses. The IDEA Connect Summer Market takes place at the end of the IDEA Mississauga Summer Company program. Students get to meet customers and get sales experience before heading back to school. The IDEA Connect Summer Market features 13 student-run businesses that are part of the Summer Company program in Mississauga. Visitors can shop for goods and services at the market. They’ll get a passport and collect a stamp as they visit each business. They can enter their stamped passports into a raffle to win an IDEA gift bag.

items.title: Ternopil Park: Mississauga honours sister-city relationship through park renaming
items.summary: Mississauga City Council renames Gulleden Park to Ternopil Park. Gulleden Park, located at 3570 Havenwood Drive in Ward 3, will be renamed to Ternopil Park, recognizing the City’s twinning partnership with the City of Ternopil, Ukraine, and celebrating the contributions of Mississauga’s Ukrainian community. The renaming reflects Mississauga’s commitment to fostering international relationships that promote cultural exchange, economic cooperation and global engagement. Earlier this year, Mississauga and Ternopil formally entered into a sister-city relationship, strengthening ties between the two communities and creating new opportunities for collaboration. Ternopil Park joins Kariya Park, which was named in 1992 to honour Mississauga’s longstanding sister-city partnership with Kariya, Japan. This past June, the City celebrated the re‑opening of a revitalized Gulleden Park. This park offers a variety of features including multi‑use pickleball & tennis courts, spray pad & playground, fitness area & skateboard features as well as pollinator gardens. The western Ukrainian city has a population of 230,000 people. It’s located 490 km from Kyiv, 125 km from Lviv and 150 km from the Ukraine-Poland border. Founded in 1540, its local economy focusses on various industries such as food and processing, mechanical engineering, metal and wood processing, construction materials and tourism. The city boasts 10 universities. “The renaming of Ternopil Park is a meaningful symbol of the friendship between Mississauga and Ternopil and of the strong ties we are building through our sister-city partnership. ” – Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish “This park is located beside St. Sofia Byzantine Catholic Elementary School and within a neighbourhood that is home to many residents of Ukrainian heritage.

items.title: Fall into fun with City programs and activities
items.summary: Discover swimming, skating, sports, arts, winter camps and more to help you learn, play and connect this season. Sweater weather, colourful leaves and busy community centres are all part of the usual fall season in Mississauga. With fall registration just around the corner, now is the perfect time to plan a season filled with fitness, swimming, skating, arts, sports and other fun programs. Whether you’re looking to build a new skill, stay active, discover a new hobby or help your child learn something new, the City of Mississauga’s fall recreation and culture programs offer something for everyone. Residents can begin browsing and bookmarking programs on August 4 and create wish lists in advance to register early, as many popular programs fill quickly. Registration opens for residents on August 11. The City of Mississauga provides programs in safe, inclusive and welcoming spaces for all ages and abilities, and supporting different interests, skill levels and accessibility needs. People of all ages and abilities, ranging from preschool-aged children to older adults. Registration for fall recreation and culture programs and winter camps. The programs are delivered by qualified staff, with children’s programs guided by the HIGH FIVE® quality standard to help ensure positive, high-quality recreation experiences. Browse programs, create wish lists and register through Active Mississauga. In-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours. City programs offer more than just a weekly activity to add to a busy schedule. They provide opportunities to stay physically active and support overall health and well-being.

items.title: Council recap: July 29, 2026
items.summary: Highlights from Mississauga’s City Council meeting. City Council approved the following at its meeting. Watch the meeting. Council directed staff to review planning policies and regulations for major digital infrastructure facilities, including artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. Staff will also prepare an Interim Control By-law that could temporarily pause new facilities while the review is completed. The review will look at land use planning, environmental impacts, energy and water use, public health, economic benefits and community impacts before future large-scale facilities are considered. Council directed staff to review Mississauga’s Adequate Temperature By-law and report back on ways to strengthen cooling requirements in apartment buildings. The review comes as extreme heat events become more common and will focus on improving tenant safety and access to cooling. Staff will examine indoor temperature standards, cooling amenity spaces and access to cooling during extended periods of hot weather. Council approved a grant-in-lieu of development charges to support an expansion at Seva Food Bank. The project will add a new mezzanine to the organization’s Wolfedale Road facility, increasing space for food bank operations, meal programs and other support services. Building on Council’s 2023 declaration of food insecurity as a crisis, the funding will help offset development-related costs for upgrades that support Mississauga residents.
